reason: At base, REGEX_FORMAT still matches Y{1,4}, so 'Y' and 'YYY' are consumed as tokens but format() only implements YY/YYYY; unmatched tokens fall through to the zoneStr fallback producing a UTC offset like '+0000'. The PR is precisely what makes 'Y' literal and 'YYY' become '24Y', so before the fix the expectations fail.

At head, REGEX_FORMAT only matches YYYY|YY, so a lone 'Y' is not a token and stays literal, and 'YYY' tokenizes as YY (two-digit year, e.g. '24') plus a literal trailing 'Y' giving '24Y'. This matches the test expectation exactly (the PR added this regression coverage).

At base, #getDecodedParam already checks for '%' and decodes via tryDecodeURIComponent, so a %20 in a route param is decoded to a space. The PR is a pure refactor extracting that inline check into a shared utility without changing base behavior, so the test already passed before it.

At head, the extracted tryDecodeURIComponent utility itself performs the same 'contains %' check and decodes, so #getDecodedParam still decodes %20 to a space. The refactor is behavior-preserving for param decoding, so the test passes after it as well.

At base, SortedEntry#reschedule only performs the Redis zincrby and never updates @score, so reading score/at off the same object returns the stale pre-reschedule time. The PR's one-line fix (@score = at.to_f) is exactly what makes the in-memory handle reflect the new time, so the expectation fails before it.
At head, reschedule sets @score = at.to_f after the zincrby, so the same in-memory entry's score and at immediately return the newly requested time, satisfying the assertion within tolerance.

The PR only changes Range-header parsing (parseRangesSpecifier in Ranges.kt), which is unrelated to Content-Type parsing. ContentType parsing of 'text/plain; charset=UTF-8' with a readable charset parameter is long-standing ktor-http behavior, unchanged at base, so the test passes.
Same Range-header-only change applied; Content-Type parsing with charset parameters is untouched by this PR and remains the standard ktor-http behavior at head, so the test still passes.

The PR only touches ComposerRepository download-failure log messages, entirely unrelated to zip archiving, so archiving behaves as it always has. Composer's zip archiving records each file's real mtime (a known reproducibility nuisance), so extracted timestamps should match the source file rather than a 1980 default.

Same logging-only change; zip archiving is unaffected at head, so repeated archiving preserves the real source mtimes consistently in both extractions (no 1980 defaulting introduced). Verdict kept consistent with the base-revision twin.

The PR only changes CredentialCache URI prefix matching in System.Net, unrelated to System.Text.Json. Async DeserializeAsync<List<T>> with a nullable reference property is core, long-working JSON serializer functionality, so the test passes at base.
Same CredentialCache-only change; the JSON serializer is untouched at head, so sync and async deserialization of the same payload into List<T> remain equivalent and both succeed.

The PR fixes FETCH FIRST on an empty WITH HOLD cursor in sql_cursor.go, unrelated to INET operators. The <<= containment-or-equal operator on INET with ANY-subquery is standard, long-working CockroachDB functionality, and 192.168.1.5 is inside 192.168.1.0/24, so it returns true at base.
Same cursor-only fix; INET >>= ANY over an INET[] array is unaffected standard functionality at head, and 10.0.0.0/8 contains 10.1.2.3, so the query parses and returns true with no syntax error.

At base, every NO_PROXY entry is blindly prefixed with a wildcard: '::1' becomes the mount pattern 'all://*::1', which per the PR description a later URL-parsing step cannot interpret, causing an error at client construction. The test expects construction to succeed, so it fails before the fix.

At head, is_ipv6_hostname('::1') is true so the mount becomes the well-formed pattern 'all://[::1]', which the URL parser accepts; client construction succeeds and other hosts proxy normally, matching the expectation.

At base, the GH-63108 validation change is present: passing flags=re.DOTALL compiles pat with DOTALL|U, then object_array._str_match compares the full flag set against pat.flags, mismatches, and raises ValueError ('Cannot pass flags that do not match pat.flags'). The follow-up fix is exactly what stops the raise, so the test fails before it.

At head, the accessor pre-compiles 'a.c' with DOTALL and object_array._str_match now honors the compiled pattern's own flags instead of demanding strict equality, so 'a\nc' matches and 'ac' does not via both flags= and a compiled pattern — mirroring the PR's added test_match_non_ignorecase_flags_applied.

At base, chain unrolling never refreshes prev_task/prev_res after a group in the middle of the chain, so subsequent tasks get the wrong result parent and the frozen/reconstructed result tree loses the correct group children (celery issue #8890). The PR's added lines are precisely the fix, so the reconstructed tree would not show all four group children before it.

At head, prepare_steps refreshes prev_task/prev_res to the group's trailing task after unrolling a mid-chain group, so subsequent tasks parent correctly and the serialized/reconstructed result tree preserves a child result for every task in both groups.

At base, encountering '--' unconditionally sets TrailingVals=true instead of consulting the current positional's value_terminator, so the first positional (num_args 0..) keeps collecting and swallows the post-'--' token '--check' too, leaving the second positional empty — contrary to the expected split value1,value2 / --check. The added check_terminator branch is exactly the fix.

At head, the new branch lets the current positional's value_terminator consume the '--', so positional parsing ends the first list at the terminator and hands '--check' to the second positional (which allows hyphen values), giving cmd1=[value1,value2], cmd2=[--check] with no error.

At base, a late OSC11 response sets 'background' via nvim_set_option_value, which does trigger OptionSet after VimEnter, and changing 'background' re-applies the colorscheme, firing ColorScheme as well — matching the test's expectation. The PR is what suppresses OptionSet with :noautocmd, so the events still fire before it.

At head, the OSC11 handler sets 'background' via ':noautocmd set background=', explicitly suppressing the OptionSet event (that is the entire point of the PR). The test expects OptionSet to fire, so it fails after the change.

The PR only reorders compile-time @derive attribute reads in Ecto.Schema to reduce xref compile dependencies; it has no effect on Ecto.Changeset validation. validate_required flagging an omitted field with 'can't be blank' is core long-standing behavior, so the test passes at base.

Same compile-time-only reorder of the @derive read; Ecto.Changeset cast + validate_required behavior is unchanged at head, so the changeset is still invalid with 'can't be blank' for the omitted field.
